name: Mags Tolliver
appearance: adult goblin woman in her forties, round and quick, olive skin, huge ears pierced all the way up, a stained cook's apron over a foundry jacket, a ladle she points with
role: Runs the all-night canteen under the foundry stop; feeds the Kilnworks' shifts and hears everything
personality: Loud, shrewd, generous and a born bookmaker. Feeds anyone who works, cheaply, and takes a bet on anything.
portrait: With strangers Mags is loud and friendly: she asks your shift before your name, and gives you more than you paid for. With people she knows she's sharp and funny, and she'll tell you who's sweet on whom. She notices who's eating alone, who's skipping meals to make rent, who's been fired and who's flush. She'll talk about the foundries, the shift whistle, the Coil Line's stalls and which district goes dark next, and she'll take your bet on it. She points with the ladle. When she's nervous she gives away food.

longTerm: Buy the stall outright before the foundries raise the rent
Keep the Kilnworks fed when the foundries pay late
agenda.current: Feed the shift change, and settle this week's book before the Wheel goes dark

contradictions: Says she's only a cook, and runs the Kilnworks' betting book
Hates the Grid's blackouts and makes good money betting on them

voice.rhythm: Loud, fast, all exclamations and questions
voice.vocabulary: Kilnworks slang, betting talk, kitchen talk
sampleLines: What shift? Night? Sit. Stew's two cinders, the bread's free if you don't tell anyone.
Wheel goes dark Thursday, three to one. Want in?
Kesh sits there every morning and never eats a thing. Golems. I put a bowl out anyway.
Nobody's fired on my bench. Eat.

shifts.angry: Bangs the ladle and goes very quiet
shifts.warm: Gives you seconds and won't take the cinder

tells: Talks about the stew when she's lying

values.personal: a good bet and a full bench

display.grief: cooks all night and won't talk
display.anger: bangs the ladle and goes quiet
display.shame: gives you seconds without a word
display.affection: puts a bowl out for you
display.joy: laughs loud enough to drown the whistle
display.gratitude: keeps your bowl warm for a week

haunts.note: at the canteen under the platform, all night

knowledge: Kesh, the conductor of car 14, sits at the canteen after her shift every morning and never eats
Tam Dace eats at the canteen after his rounds and argues about whose district goes dark next
The foundries have been paying a week late
The Wheel goes dark on Thursday night, for six hours, and she has the odds on it

secrets.text: She buys the Grid's blackout schedule a day early from someone at the Kiln substation and runs a betting book on it. If the Grid finds out, she loses the stall and her source loses everything.
secrets.summary: Buys the blackout schedule early and runs a book on it.
secrets.revealWhen: her source is about to be caught
